govdocs-archive_org-mazdean-critique-of-: The old Persian doubt-chaser — Mardanfarrokh’s book — takes on the new faith. The 800s pleader backs the fire-faith. The faith of Zoroaster was at stake. The book is a landmark of god-rows. Its pleas are keen and book-learned. Few such books live on.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CookBook_Cook_B: This National Chicken Cooking Contest Finals flyer — from Delmarva Poultry Industry — is a food-industry handout. The file belongs to the business archive. Cooking contests drew crowds and sponsors. The contest was a yearly event. The item is a fragment of trade history.
the-2002-cia-world-factbook: Every year the Central Intelligence Agency publishes this thick reference volume profiling nearly every country on earth. Each entry packs in geography, population, government, economy, and military facts in compact tables and short notes. Researchers, students, and the simply curious have long used the Factbook as a quick, reliable snapshot of the world as it stood in 2002.
the-bobbsey-twins-at-meadow-brook: Laura Lee Hope takes Nan, Bert, Freddie, and Flossie Bobbsey to the country in this cheerful series installment. At Meadow Brook the twins enjoy farm fun, new friends, and a mild mystery to solve. Generations of young readers grew up with the Bobbseys, whose wholesome adventures made them among the most beloved children in American books.
favorite-dishes-a-columbian-autograph-so: Compiled for the 1893 Columbian Exposition in Chicago, this souvenir cookbook gathers favorite recipes contributed — and autographed — by famous women of the day. Beyond its practical dishes, the book is a social document of the fair that introduced America to the modern world. A tasty piece of history.
the-grey-fairy-book: Andrew Lang's Grey Fairy Book gathers thirty-five tales from around the world — French, German, Italian, and more exotic sources. Princes, giants, and clever youngest sons populate stories chosen for their strangeness and charm. Part of Lang's beloved rainbow of fairy books, it has delighted children for over a century.
miss-parloa-s-new-cook-book: Maria Parloa — America's first celebrity cooking teacher — offers hundreds of tested recipes in this comprehensive guide. From soups to desserts, her clear instructions brought professional standards to home kitchens. A landmark of American cookery and a fascinating record of what the nation ate.
the-belgian-cookbook: Compiled for wartime relief, this Belgian cookbook offers the hearty dishes of little Belgium — stews, mussels, and Flemish favorites. Its sale aided refugees of the Great War. Good food for a good cause. Waterzooi, carbonnades, and waffles share these pages, each recipe a small act of mercy.
the-green-fairy-book: Andrew Lang's Green Fairy Book gathers tales from many lands — Spanish, Chinese, and more — in his beloved colored series. Magic, wit, and wonder fill its pages. A childhood treasure for over a century. Dragons, fairies, and clever youngest sons await within its covers.
